sources.text: For 25 years, XBOX has remained focused on building games players love, and our anniversary year has been a particularly strong example. From Gears of War: E-Day , Forza Horizon 6 , and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , to hugely anticipated games like Fable , players have more great games to play on XBOX than ever. Today, The Game Awards has announced this year’s list of nominees and titles across XBOX’s creative teams have earned eight nominations across multiple categories. Outside of gaming, Prime Video’s ‘Fallout’ has been nominated for Best Adaptation. Thank you to all of the teams that brought these great games to players. Voting is now open on The Game Awards’ official site – tune into The Game Awards on December 10 to see if your favorite games from 2026 take home an award. Our publishing partners also received nominations across a range of categories, with many games available to play today with Game Pass. 007 First Light and CONTROL Resonant are both nominated for Game of the Year and playable across devices with XBOX Play Anywhere. Game Pass subscribers can play nominees like Gears of War: E-Day , Forza Horizon 6 , No Man’s Sky , and more. See below for the full list of nominees playable on XBOX, including Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , and remember you can vote for your favorites right now over at TheGameAwards.com . In the meantime, many of these titles will be available at their lowest prices yet with XBOX’s Black Friday sale, starting November 19 – find out more here . Congratulations to this year’s incredible nominees!

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI chega amanhã, dia 19 de novembro
sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Review
sources.text: During my first dozen-or-so hours with Grand Theft Auto 6, I fixed my leaky roof, collected some rum from a shady liquor store, played way too many games of pool, read a book about World War 2 soldiers with a penchant for teabagging, and caught a lot of fish. On the more ridiculous end of the spectrum, I also temporarily… borrowed a luxury yacht called Party on the Poop Deck before running it aground and drinking its owner’s beer, slapped the crap out of a bloke who cursed at me, found a finger in my horniest neighbour’s plumbing, threatened an alligator wearing a hat, and got mugged by a drunk sea captain with a harpoon gun – before stealing his weapon while he peed in a garden. Over 100 hours later, I’ve now completely lost track of all the things I’ve seen and done within GTA 6’s astounding open world – and I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend here, endlessly exploring and interacting with Vice City and the massive area surrounding it. While the well-paced story effectively nudged me around the map, there are still vast sections of it that I’m yet to even visit – despite hitting the credits after almost 120 hours of hijinks. Frankly, I’ve never played anything that’s hit quite like GTA 6 – and right now I have zero plans to stop playing it. Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are an interesting pair of playable characters, and unlike any leads that have come before them in the series. Their motivations and goals are very different from the main characters of previous GTA games, and their priority is really about escape rather than revenge or empire building. They’re not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story – which unfolds like four or five seasons of a prestige TV show. My Jason and Lucia maintained a professional criminal rating throughout thanks to my style of play, where I opt for clean escapes, stealth, and non-lethal takedowns against general law enforcement if feasible, disabling vehicles by popping tyres rather than pummelling the windscreens with gunfire, and leaving civilians unharmed as often as possible. By the end of the story, I had actually only killed 11 civilians, all of which would’ve been unfortunate accidents. Jason, a capable yet calm and softly spoken army veteran, is a natural fit for GTA. He remains mostly a mystery throughout, but his quiet cowboy demeanour doesn’t stray too far from Red Dead Redemption 2’s Arthur Morgan, and I like that. Lucia, who’s headstrong but not abrasive and confident but not cocky, gets to showcase a wider range of emotions. She’s easily the most likeable and multifaceted woman in the history of the series, and it’s abundantly clear that GTA’s writing has grown up dramatically in the last 13 years – and that RDR2 has had nothing but positive effects on its sister series. We play mostly as Jason for the opening phase of Chapter 1, but it’s a smart way of easing us into the many systems we need to come to grips with (there’s a full help menu to explain any controls or actions you might forget). In the time it takes to start and finish many typical shooters and action games, I’d lived several days of a second life as Jason, who spends a good deal of his time on the wrong side of the law couriering drug shipments up and down the Leonida Keys but otherwise keeps a low profile in the relatively quiet tourist town he calls home. There’d been strife and there’d been shootouts, sure, but the main thread of the story had barely begun: Lucia was yet to re-enter the picture, I’d not even visited Vice City itself at all, and I was entirely content to while away hours messing around with GTA 6’s many, many distractions. It’s ironic, perhaps, that some of its greatest distractions are actually games themselves – Jason has a PlayStation-style console in his home featuring three playable games, and his local bar has a darkly humorous riff on classic Buck Hunter cabinets I kept getting sucked into. Straight away, it’s evident this is not a world of painted-on backdrops and empty props. This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I’ve ever played, and it’s one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series. Yes, it was a long wait, but believe me when I say Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out (which, handily enough, is also something you can do yourself in GTA 6 if you find yourself beached). I’ll readily admit I’m an easy mark for a game like this. I love action movies, car chases, and dad rock, and GTA 6 holds precisely the same things near and dear. I won’t list the long catalogue of movie references I’ve spotted since it’s way more satisfying to recognise them yourself. I also won’t spoil any of the specific needle drops Rockstar finds itself indulging in more than ever – one of which has become one of my favourite moments in the entire series. It does take over the dial a bit more than usual for key moments, but it’s always to great effect, and it certainly hasn’t come at the cost of any reduced focus on radio stations. The mammoth tracklist otherwise includes the return of classic stations V-Rock, Emotion, and Vice City FM, all of which are absolutely overflowing with solid gold (as is new metal station The Chamber). Just those four stations alone – which account for the lion’s share of my listening – feature nearly 200 songs between them. In a considerable blow for any company trying to sell me a next-generation console in the near future, GTA 6 also looks even better than it sounds. Allow me to freely concede I’ve never been fussy about frame rates, so long as they don’t constantly fluctuate. For all the hand-wringing I’ve observed over the fact that GTA 6 is locked to 30 frames-per-second – just as Rockstar’s most recent cowboy masterpiece was, not for nothing – I simply did not care i

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 | Critical Consensus
sources.text: Critics praise the "richly drawn and compelling romance" of Jason and Lucia in GTA 6, delivering a record Metacritic score After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been met with universal acclaim. Despite a lead-up marred by delays and leaks the hype has only grown, with over 17 million pre-orders generating more than $1.6 billion in revenue, according to recent data . Critics have spent weeks exploring Rockstar's Leonida, featuring the Bonnie-and-Clyde-inspired duo Jason and Lucia, leading to a Metacritic score of 99 . Backed by over 100 reviews, the title is currently listed as the platform's best game of all time , above the original N64 release of The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time. In the words of The Guardian 's Keza MacDonald: "Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have seen yet." "Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming [...] and contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start." IGN 's Luke Reilly emphasised that the wait for GTA 6 was reflected in the detail Rockstar has poured into its world. "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played, and it's one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series," he said. "Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out.” The game's level of detail raised concerns about performance, particularly its 30fps cap on all consoles , including the PlayStation 5 Pro. However, Reilly found that this limitation did not diminish the experience. "What matters to me is that it looks absolutely incredible and runs smoothly and reliably on a standard PS5. I find all the brilliant visual flourishes far more important, from the concentric rings of ripples on water due to helicopter rotor downwash, to the almost imperceptible line of sweat that appears on Lucia's forehead after a brisk jog, or the buckling of the fabric on a shirt as torsos twist, to the temporary dents on a punching bag as you strike it." "If a sufficiently stable and properly paced 30fps is the route to GTA 6 looking and functioning the way it does, bug-free, then I have no complaints." GTA 6's immersion extends to daily routines that improve stats like health and stamina, or managing car fuel levels. As Game Informer 's Matt Miller observed, these activities "add pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward." These everyday moments are initially character-specific, as The New York Times' Yussef Cole noted. "Jason can opt to fix up his run-down bachelor pad in preparation for Lucia's imminent release. There are numerous tasks around the house, like putting up drywall, painting and fixing the roof, that take up the player's time and the character's in-game resources, but they aim toward a productive and satisfying goal: a better relationship." That's not to say GTA 6 isn't like past games, where violence is encouraged and chaos is one petty crime away. Miller emphasised that these moments do not detract from the "meticulously choreographed" set pieces, which "run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect." Critics agreed that GTA 6 offers unexpected emotional depth, thanks to nuance in both the representation of the lead characters and the player's ability to control them. IGN's Reilly described Jason and Lucia as "unlike any leads that have come before them in the series," whose priorities are each other and escaping the criminal life they find themselves increasingly entrenched in. "They're not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story,"he wrote. The New York Times' Cole agreed, adding that the emphasis on the duo's relationship "reflects a maturation of a series that has generally only told stories about men solipsistically chasing after their own success." He continued: "Choosing romance is the easy part, thanks to the chemistry and human characterisation of the two leads. Lucia and Jason's relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between." Game Informer's Miller described Jason and Lucia's relationship as "elevating the game to new heights, lending this instalment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries." "This is, without a doubt, video gaming's most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you're left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts." The Guardian's MacDonald "found it impossible not to care" for the couple over time. "They are our avatars in GTA 6's world, but they are not blank stand-ins for the player: you decide their actions but not their personalities. They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim [...] When the story gave me opportunities to decide what would happen next, what came to mind for me was what they would do, not what I would do." sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker pleads guilty to all charges
sources.text: Arion Kurtaj released dozens of GTA 6 videos to the public more than a year before the game was formally revealed. The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group. Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick , a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin. A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital , where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger. As we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Kurtaj was also reportedly violent while in hospital custody, causing "dozens" of reports of injuries or property damage. In July 2026, that 'no longer a danger' determination was presumably made, as Kurtaj was released from hospital and moved to prison to await retrial. He has now pleaded guilty to multiple hacks carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, including the Rockstar hack that led to the GTA 6 leak. He also pleaded guilty to assaults on workers while in custody, which the BBC report says included "multiple biting incidents." As I said when Kurtaj was moved from hospital to prison, the whole thing strikes me as odd. The big question is how Kurtaj's state of mind at the time of the crimes will influence the outcome of his guilty plea, given that a previous court determined that he needed multiple years of institutionalization. BBC tech reporter Joe Tidy, who's been following the case since Kurtaj's transfer, also described it as "an unusual move" in his report. Coincidentially, one must assume, Grand Theft Auto 6 launches for consoles on November 19. Kurtaj will be sentenced at a future date. The leaker who goes by Cyberleek , who recently distributed several GTA 6 gameplay videos apparently taken with a development build of the game, remains at large. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
sources.text: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. It's fitting I guess that GTA San Andreas is such a strange delight to return to. As I've waited, like everyone else, for GTA 6 , I've been back here in the GTA games of the past, via the slightly dodgy remasters from a few years ago. And what's come through for me, spending a few idle mornings messing around in San Andreas, a game I thought I knew pretty well, is how beautifully odd everything is now. The best part of 20 years have given a game that once strained against its host technology a genuine aesthetic. Surprisingly sparse in detailing, as angular and sheer as dream architecture, in love with expanses, San Andreas is perfectly placed, it seems to me, to capture just how weird California can be. California and Nevada. This is the part I always forget. I mainly think of San Andreas these days through the lens of GTA 5 , which gives you LA and its surroundings but lets the single city serve as the star. It has a bigger footprint than the earlier game, sure, but it uses that space to go deep on the detailing and the sense of a singular, fiercely specific place. San Andreas meanwhile offers three cities - and one of them isn't actually in California. Alongside spins on LA and San Francisco, you get a version of Las Vegas. It's quite neat really: the three points of some arcane spiritual triangle. The kind of thing Marvel Whiteside Parsons, aerospace engineer and Actual Wizard, might have scratched in the dust of his backyard to help him control the weather. He lived - and died - in Pasadena, so all this would have been familiar anyway. There is a classic moment in every GTA. A moment where the map opens up in the early games, or when you explore enough in the later games, and simply get to understand the audacity of what is being attempted here. In San Andreas, and this feels apt, the best way to have this moment is to break the rules, sneaking into the open map before the game is fully ready for you. An early mission allows you to step away from the critical path, as it were, and peg it to the airport in Los Santos, where a plane is waiting to be pinched. Taxi, feel the thrust, and you're off. LA beneath you - sorry, Los Santos - and on the horizon a dinkytown version of the Golden Gate Bridge and the MGM Grand. Dinkytown is the word. From the sky, the huge map of San Andreas, which still feels like an incredible piece of work - such ambition! - can look like toys laid out on a duvet in the remasters. Coming back from GTA 5, a masterpiece of texture, the cities of San Andreas in particular feel very weird - cramped and condensed and wonderfully stagey, arranged the way a kid might jury-rig them together from shoeboxes and stray cardboard. On your way out of Grove Street early on you pass the Los Santos equivalent of the Hollywood sign, looming so close the way it does in the movies but not in the actual city and you feel you could touch it. Downtown is reduced to a handful of the best buildings - it's always pleasing to see the one from the brilliant first act of Speed made the cut - but still manages to capture the important stuff too, which in this case is the way that modern LA looms somewhat cruelly over the old city, captured with a strange sepulchral dignity in the form of the City Hall, so easy to spot but now so small! Elsewhere, the ersatz Las Vega Strip looks like a drawing based on memory - a few of the classic shapes are there, but it's a sketch of a place. In this way, I guess, it captures a truth about Las Vegas. Also, perhaps, it's an admission that this is a town comfortably out of the reach of satire. As for San Francisco, it's a 60s cop movie delight to fishtail around. It nails the hills and what more do you need for a game with cars in it? Taken as a whole these cities feel mesmerising now. And it's the limitations that make them sing, I think: those sheer granite canyons of downtown LA with its towering blocks of architecture and surprisingly thin traffic, with only the very faintest of ambient soundtracks that ensures any gunfire will pop and clap and shake you out of your seat. (Remember, I am playing the remasters and sound effects may be missing.) This is the LA of Repo Man rather than Heat - an otherland where the buildings feel alien, even the air feels alien. At night, palm trees stand out against a sky that glows a deep, clean red. GTA 5 would finesse all of this, the skyboxes and whatnot, but perhaps in that finessing something is lost. (Both games, incidentally, have such a talent for capturing California's kitsch excess that they perhaps miss some of the sweeter truths, such as the astonishing diversity of cultures a city like Los Angeles finds homes for. But how could any game do that justice?) Dinkytowns aside, what San Andreas does better than GTA 5 is space - the peculiar flat spaces of Southern California in particular, a state in which you can never quite tell where the wilderness ends and the landscaping begins, and where the ancient rocks that announce the horizon can look new, like stage settings, while the freeways feel truly ancient, concrete lizards sleeping on the dirt, bleached by the easy sun. sources.title: Newzoo analyst expects Grand Theft Auto to turn around a rough year for console gaming: 'without GTA 6 the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026'
sources.text: Consoles cost more than ever, and even if you can afford to buy one you don't have as much left over to buy games for it as you used to. That's made 2026 an underwhelming year for console gaming sales, but according to the latest forecast from videogame market analysts Newzoo , the imminent launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will turn that around. "As we explored in the Global Games Market Report 2026," said Newzoo's director of market intelligence, Emmanuel Rosier, "without GTA VI the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026. Instead, the game's launch is expected to generate billions of dollars in revenue and give console spending a significant boost." Rosier is the analyst who, back in August, was skeptical about the idea of BioWare surviving long enough to make another Mass Effect game . I wish he'd been wrong about that, but it turned out he was right on the money with that prediction. "Western console has been losing ground," he went on to say. "Its share of global games revenue fell from 21.5% in 2015 to 17.1% in 2025, and its revenue has been broadly flat since 2021. Console adoption shows the same pattern. In Western markets, the console player base has been flat since 2022. Most people who want to play on console already do." Newzoo's prediction is that GTA 6 "will lift console full-game spending by 17.5% this year". But that's just the start of the story. "So while GTA VI is undoubtedly one of the most important releases of the decade," Rosier says, "its initial impact will be concentrated in Western console. That’s still a big market, which we forecast will be worth $36.3 billion in 2026, but it's only part of the industry. The longer-term global story will depend on what happens next, particularly on PC and online." Though tradition has plenty of people expecting a delay of roughly a year and a half between GTA 6's console and PC releases, general console malaise and the value of GTA Online—likely to be bigger on PC, and perhaps launch alongside the PC port—is a reason to think maybe the wait won't be so long. A recent GamesBeat report claims it'll be out in early 2027. "PC is far bigger than console in several major markets, including China," Rosier says, "and a PC release could expose the game to a much broader international audience. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. "The online mode is another key unknown. Depending on how it's positioned and monetized, it could significantly expand the game's audience. If Rockstar adopts a model that lowers barriers to entry, the long-term opportunity outside the traditional Western console audience could be much larger than it appears today." GTA Online was a huge part of GTA 5 's long-tail success. While Newzoo's data says at least 37% of players who preordered GTA 6 have spent money on GTA Online, only 15% did so in the last 12 months. It's in need of a refresh, and though Rockstar haven't confirmed anything, Twitch's CEO also says GTA 6's multiplayer component will be out in 2027 . sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 review
sources.text: My best attempt at summing up Grand Theft Auto 6 came from a conversation with a friend about something else entirely. This friend was telling me about a theory they'd recently heard, and half agreed with, that just so happened to layer over this game perfectly. Americans, they said, paraphrasing, have found a new 'third place': the car. I'm slightly skeptical of the obsession with third places these days - love the concept; less convinced that societal bonds are collapsing because today's men aren't spending enough time at their barber's. But here it felt just right: GTA 6 is, of course, a game both about America and about the personal vehicle. The clue's in the name. And as you play GTA 6, you realise, over and over, that the car is where so much of this game happens. It's where you take calls that lead to missions or story developments; where you pick up, hang out with, and chat to your partner; where you race away from police, gangs, wild animals and weirdos. Where you do much of your discovery of this properly, disorientatingly, astoundingly big and detailed world. Where you'll be when you find the most 'emergent events'. And, more than it's ever been before, the car is now an essential partner in itself; a place to stow weapons, disguises, and stolen goods - a companion it feels almost impossible to do without. I could go on about this. GTA 6 is a game of perpetual motion, as protagonists Jason and Lucia do their best to outrun a world that so often feels a step ahead - and which often culminates in some of the most exhilarating, astonishing chase sequences ever built in a video game. GTA 5 , its Los Santos-set predecessor, was aware enough of the importance of the car to name an in-game canyon after Reyner Banham, the British architectural critic who described Los Angeles' freeway system, one of the city's "four ecologies", as "Autopia". So yes: the car is the third place, in modern America and in GTA 6. The place of self-actualisation between work and home - two points that, for GTA 6's protagonists in particular, seem to always be in a state of flux. Maybe the car's their true home. For the longest time I really thought that idea summed up GTA 6 quite nicely. Until I didn't. Reducing GTA 6 to just the car, I realised, looking at it through only that one lens, forces you to be too narrow. You miss too much of it. What about the romance? The sensuality? The people and the natural world? And so what I've come to settle on instead - and honestly I expect this to change many more times over the coming days and weeks too, as even more of this horizonless game rolls back to reveal itself - is that GTA 6 just doesn't have a single thread to pull on. No one thing that, when properly grasped, suddenly draws it into a manageable shape. I've no doubt we'll all try. People have, for whatever reason, always reached for the most reductive ideas when they talk about Grand Theft Auto in particular. Maybe it's a natural response to something too big and unwieldy to instantly get your head around: to seize the first acceptable idea and declare it just 'x' . To admit something is too complex for you to immediately summarise is far less comfortable than simply dismissing it on the spot. Whatever it is, GTA 6 isn't just anything. For one, every thing it is also seems to have an opposite. It's vast - incomprehensibly vast - but also overloaded with miniscule detail. It's about big ideas, themes, places - America, society, love - and also about individuals. It's ridiculous and puerile, and also sometimes mature. Tender and violent. Deep and shallow. Novel and, in places, surprisingly familiar. It's both a big adventure playground of video game activities and a focused story of suffocating intensity. Whatever foible might arise, the game presents you with a ready-made answer - often quite literally: you can turn off notifications about your relationship status in the menu if you just want to ignore that part. You can switch to the old controls (GTA 6 has seen a bit of a control overhaul), from the first screen you're shown. Or simply tear off in the opposite direction to whatever it is that dissatisfies you and do something else. If there's an idea to reduce this game to, then, the best I can manage is this: maybe Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game designed to be irreducible. None of that is to say it's perfect. It's easy to stand in front of something like this and just bask in the awe of it, forgetting to stop a moment and step back. The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome, but there are also nits to pick. But then you step back again and they tend to fade away. GTA 6 will not be for everyone. But no game has made a better attempt at being everything. GTA 6's story begins with Jason and Lucia. Discussing it beyond that is, frankly, almost impossible to do with any kind of substance without also spoiling it. For all the precipitous leaks, Rockstar has kept its story's two most essential moments - its beginning and its end - entirely secret, and without those two moments we're only really left with euphemisms. Jason and Lucia are on the run, after a seemingly simple fetch quest goes awry. Who they're running from, or why they're being chased quite so hard, remains agonisingly beyond their field of view. But what is clear, right from the off, is exactly why they're so determined to escape. And amongst all this Rockstar has achieved something kind of momentous, when it comes to Grand Theft Auto: we've got real and very human stakes. What else can be said? Well, let's go back to Rockstar's decision to begin so explicitly with Jason and Lucia. This is a story about a relationship. You can nurture or neglect it, but fundamentally that relationship - however strong - is at the heart of things. sources.text: Thirteen years later, Rockstar has crafted a worthy successor to GTA V and the new standard-bearer for open-world games. How do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V ? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade. That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA . A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. At a time when much of the video game industry is struggling , the next edition of GTA stands alone , a cultural moment so big ( almost ) everybody has been forced to get out of the way . The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI ’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen. Even more remarkable? The game was actually worth the wait. At this point I’ve spent nearly 80 hours in Leonida, GTA VI ’s fictional take on Florida. And what I’ve experienced is a game that combines the wide-open freedom offered in GTA V with the remarkable level of immersion from the studio’s 2018 release Red Dead Redemption 2 , while also improving on both qualities. At the same time, it’s also the most mature GTA game Rockstar has ever made, merging the criminal antics and absurdist humor the series is known for with a love story that gives you new ways to interact with the world and new reasons for wanting to push forward. This is the GTA game the studio has been building toward for its entire existence. Let’s start with that new premise. GTA V introduced the idea of multiple protagonists to the series, and VI takes that concept in a different direction. It’s a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired story about Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals who meet while, of course, stealing a car. It’s the most GTA -possible meet-cute. The idea is that you can play as both characters individually and also build their relationship over the course of the game. Things start out relatively slow. At the outset, Lucia is in prison, and you play solely as Jason, getting things ready for when she gets out. You can fix up your ramshackle house — that involves actually nailing down new stairs and rolling out paint on the walls — and also start building up a nest egg through means that are not exactly legal. Jason and Lucia’s relationship grows naturally over the course of the game, but it’s also a slow buildup to becoming the inseparable pair they were by the end of my playthrough. GTA VI approaches most of the experience with confident and deliberate pacing. Even when you control them individually, the characters are often together, either just hanging out or partnering for a crime. And being able to play as both is one of the game’s standout features. But I didn’t get to that point in the game until almost 17 hours in. Before that, you play as both leads mostly solo, learning who they are as people, before you’re given free rein to switch between the two. What’s great about the premise is how seamlessly it fits with what you’re actually doing in the game. There’s some bigger-picture stuff that I won’t spoil, but generally speaking, the main goal in GTA VI is to make a lot of money so that Jason and Lucia can get out of the criminal life for good and retire somewhere comfortably. And outside of the big story missions, you’re largely free to choose how you go about that. You can rob jewelry stores, steal cars, raid drug dens, or even search for hidden treasure at the bottom of the sea. Over the course of the game you’ll also meet different criminals who serve as fences, so you can sell them whatever you’ve got to build up your savings account. Sometimes they’ll even text you targets that are particularly lucrative. The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. I’m not a big fan of armed robbery, for instance. There are just so many things that can go wrong, and I almost always end up killing some innocent bystander when I try to escape. But I love getaway chases, and so stealing cars became my main form of income. Most importantly, though, this structure gives you a lot of reasons to go out in the world and explore. The missions take you all over the map — which is actually entirely accessible from the very beginning, if you choose to play that way — including not only the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City, but also tourist beaches, swamps, trailer parks, and a wild variety of other locations, each with its own landscape to explore and characters to meet. To be clear: Despite being larger, more mature, and more lifelike, this is still very much GTA . This is a game about chaos and crime. This comes across in a few ways. First, there are those smaller missions where you never really know how things will play out. The cashier at the pawn shop you’re robbing might have a shotgun, or you might accidentally smash into a big rig during a high-speed getaway. The world itself is full of unpredictable moments that force you to think on your feet. Several times I stopped my car to talk to an NPC whose vehicle broke down on the side of the road. In one instance the driver just swore at me to leave her alone. In another, I got pulled into an entire storyline involving a delivery driver who needed help to keep her AI chatbot manager off her back. I delivered her packages and ended up dealing with everything from porch pirates to tigers. The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. There are also the multistep heists, which return from GTA V more intricate and complex. sources.text: GTA 6 is a game that at times feels almost embarrassingly expensive and extravagant. I cleaned a boat with a pressure washer and watched the suds build up realistically in the concrete below my characterâs flip-flops. I ran through a tram station and spotted over 100 different NPCs milling about, all unique and all moving. Hair gets wet. Sweat builds up on backs. Even for Rockstar, the master of tiny details, GTA 6 is overflowing with examples of what happens when you let a studio work on one game for a decade. Itâs a lot, but it all serves the purpose of creating a virtual world that players can truly get lost in.Â Iâve put over 150 hours into GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 Pro, and I expect Iâll spend even more time in this digital recreation of Florida and Miami, as thereâs so much to do and see in Vice City. I doubt most players will see half of it. I bet I wonât ever see it all.Â GTA 6 is a massive third-person open-world game, like Rockstarâs previous offerings. It merges the slower pace and slice-of-life mechanics from Red Dead Redemption 2 with the urban sprawl and crime-movie feel of GTA IV and GTA V . Itâs a more grounded journey than its predecessors, one which requires more planning and consideration if you want to survive and succeed as modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, robbing small stores as you work your way up to bigger scores, like banks. Itâs often a tougher game than any past GTA , but in a way that rewards skill and patience. Or bravery, stupidity, and luck.Â I have quibbles about some clunky controls and some story pacing problems in the gameâs later chapters, but like crappy cupholders in a million-dollar supercar, they donât really get in the way of what’s here. Instead, they’re minor issues to point at as I hit the gas and go 200 MPH with the radio blasting.Â The best part of Grand Theft Auto 6 isnât what I expected. It’s not the crime, or the action, or the massive world to explore, though all of those parts are excellent and better than ever. The real standout of GTA 6 , the part of the game that kept me hooked and which I wonât forget anytime soon, is its central duo, Jason and Lucia. Not only do they have very different motivations than past GTA protagonists, wanting to create a better life for themselves and escape their life of crime instead of vying to become crime lords or get revenge, but they are easily Rockstarâs most fully fleshed-out, believable, and relatable characters. At the start of the game, Jason and Lucia are separated after a short relationship. Lucia tried to rob a payday loan place after breaking up with Jason and, in the process, got arrested. This moment has huge ramifications for both of their lives and ultimately pulls them together early on in GTA 6 âs runtime. Jason, an Army vet, is more reserved than your average GTA protagonist. Heâs a loyal man who’s conflicted about the things he does to get by and try to make things better for himself and Lucia. A lot of people tell Jason heâs a good guy, but heâs never sure if he really is. Meanwhile, Lucia, a petty thief living paycheck to paycheck, knows sheâs flawed and doesnât care nearly as much as Jason about that fact. Sheâs more focused on improving her life by any means and has a bigger goal that drives her to take bigger risks.Â Together they balance each other out, with Jason often acting as a voice of reason and Lucia pushing him to strive for more. Their dynamic is unlike anything Iâve seen in a Rockstar-developed game, and thanks to some stellar writing and performances, I found myself deeply caring about these two criminals just trying to make it.Â Throughout the entire run of GTA 6 , Jason and Lucia interact as you would expect two real people who care for each other would. They joke with each other, comment on events happening around them, share secrets, and help each other when they can.Â Spending time with them is never annoying. Neither Lucia nor Jason pesters the player when youâre hanging around with them in the open world. Sometimes they might point out that you missed a turn or a possible way to sneak into a gang-infested hideout. This never felt like some annoying video-gamey handholding, just a couple working together.Â While Jason and Lucia are both skilled at stealing cars, shooting guns, and running around causing chaos, they arenât always treated as equals in the world. While playing as Lucia, I was hit on by random assholes and catcalled by men on the street. It wasnât constant, but it happened enough that it was impossible to ignore. Some characters will also doubt Luciaâs abilities, but never question Jasonâs skills as a murderous criminal. It adds an intriguing wrinkle to playing as either character. Jason often has her back in these scenarios, but lets her hold her own, and she does so with sharp words and strong punches.Â Even outside of when they directly speak to each other to tell stories or give feedback, the other’s presence is always felt, sometimes in small gestures, like one holding the door for the other as they enter a building. sources.text: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time . Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans. But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players. It took 13 years , a reported 10-figure budget, and the weight of the world’s expectations, but Grand Theft Auto VI is here. And it’s fantastic . The Verge ’s Andrew Webster takes a break from the game to tell us all about life in Vice City, and why GTA VI ’s approach to coffee tells us everything we need to know. Lost in the excitement of GTA VI finally launching is the fact that Rockstar employees are in the process of voting on whether or not to unionize. Developer Nestor Uriarte explains the importance of the moment in an essay in The Guardian : Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that. As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more. Now that reviews have dropped for the game, it has skyrocketed to the top of Metacritic’s highest-rated list , surpassing Ocarina of Time (the original, not the remake ). Of course, this could change as more reviews trickle in, but for now it’s safe to say that GTA VI was worth the long wait. Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the biggest GTA game to date; it’s also the most romantic. Though the series is well known for its sordid assortment of criminal leads, GTA VI switches things up by starring a pair of thieves who also happen to fall in love after meeting while stealing a car. It’s still an open-world action game full of chaos and mayhem. But many players will also be attempting to nurture the budding relationship in between heists. The sprawling game is designed to support both audiences. “It’s a risk,” explains Rob Nelson, producer on GTA VI and co-studio head at developer Rockstar North. “It’s a real change for Grand Theft Auto . You can still play it the old way, you can reject all of this stuff. But for people who do engage, it’s meaningful — you’re earning it, you’re working at it, just like in a normal relationship.” How do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V ? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade. That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA . A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. Sony has confirmed the 1.267GB download is mandatory to play the new Grand Theft Auto when it launches at midnight tonight. As with most PlayStation firmware patches, we don’t know what it does though, beyond “some security fixes to the system software.” Rockstar hasn’t publicly said who is playing the two leads in GTA VI , but The Game Awards’ nominee video says that Manni L. Perez has been nominated for Best Performance for her work in the game. GTA VI earned eight nominations , the most of any title, including one for Game of the Year . Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other big companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS says.

sources.text: GTA 6 has become the joint-highest rated game of all time, following the widespread publication of reviews in the past hour. Rockstar's masterpiece currently sits with an all-time best score of 99 on Metacritic , an honor shared only with Nintendo's original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time release back in 1997 on N64, almost 30 years ago. No other game since has managed such a feat. (The new version of Ocarina for Switch 2 managed a paltry score of just 96.) While both the N64 version of Ocarina and GTA 6 share a 99 average, GTA 6 has impressively managed to pull this off with more than six times' the number of reviews — over 120 at the time of writing, with over 100 of those listed with a perfect score. And while it's possible GTA 6's ranking could still slip down a point as more reviews are published, it would still be the best-rated game in nearly three decades. Few others titles released in the recent memory have come anywhere close to this — though if you head back to the last console generation, Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Super Mario Odyssey both managed a 97 average, a standing they share with Rockstar's own Red Dead Redemption 2. IGN's GTA 6 review is of course now live, and also returned a perfect 10/10 score. We described it as "exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered," as well as "unprecedented, unbelievable and unmissable." sources.title: GTA 6 Xbox Series S Performance: How Does the Weakest Console Handle the Biggest Game of All Time?
sources.text: GTA 6 is finally here , and one of the biggest questions heading up to launch is how well the Xbox Series S would handle the game – well, I've finally had the chance to play the game on the tiny Xbox. Rockstar announced a couple weeks ago that all versions of GTA 6 would be 'targeting' 30 fps , and while it's disappointing that even the PS5 Pro won't be able to hit 60 fps, that performance is about what I expected from the Xbox Series S. And while I wait for my framerate analysis to stop running on my first clip of the game, the Xbox Series S version actually seems pretty decent, all things considered. The Xbox Series S obviously doesn't have the same graphics treats that the PS5 Pro version of the game has, but even without the ray traced shadows and the PSSR, the game holds up well on the 1440p machine. Character models are still extremely detailed, and even has some decent subsurface scattering and the environments are incredibly beautiful, no doubt learning from Rockstar's time with Red Dead Redemption 2. But where the Xbox Series S falls short is in the finer details. The edge of nearly every surface is aliased, almost looking like there's a border of static around every character and building, particularly around people's hair. There's also an early scene on a boat, where Jason's face is noticeably soft until it zooms closer in, no doubt to save on some GPU resources. But, GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S is using FSR 4 to upscale from 720p up to 1080p, so some softness is to be expected. Through the intro of the game, GTA 6 typically sits right at 30 fps on the Xbox Series S, and it's surprisingly smooth. However, there are certain parts of the game – like when Lucia pulls out a gun in one of the first scenes – where the frame rate drops. Usually, these drops are very minor, but I did notice a couple of drops as low as 24 fps, according to Trdrop. However, I will say that I didn't really notice most of the drops. I didn't get early access to GTA 6, so all of this is based on the first section of the game. The real test of GTA 6's performance is going to be how it handles some of the wild scenes that are sure to come in the later parts fo the game. But, any action game needs to nail the calmer moments if it wants any chance of standing up when you're surrounded by explosions and gunfire, and when it comes to GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S, it mostly nails that baseline. The game looks great, considering the level of hardware available, but you will definitely notice the difference if you put it side-by-side with something like the PS5 Pro. As GTA 6's launch unfolds, we'll be live blogging the game , watching for all the weird and wild stuff that the community finds. IGN also gave GTA 6 a perfect 10, where reviewer Luke Reilly calls it "exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played. " For everything else GTA 6, stay tuned to IGN. Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. sources.text: The 13-year wait for Grand Theft Auto 6 pays off After more than a decade of waiting, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. Rockstar Games' new open-world crime adventure game is playable by the masses — at least in some parts of the world — and has been playable by critics for some time. GTA 6 's review embargo lifted on Wednesday, Nov. 18, and more than a hundred reviews have been tabulated by Metacritic. The consensus is clear: GTA 6 is "monumental," "unbelievably fun," and "truly remarkable," critics say. The overwhelmingly positive critical response has helped GTA 6 set a new record: It's now the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic , where it currently sits above the previous title-holder, the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . GTA 6 currently has a 99 Metascore (out of 100), the same score that Metacritic displays for Ocarina of Time . The latter score is based on just 22 critic reviews of the Nintendo 64 game. GTA 6 's Metascore is based on more than 150. Both the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X versions of Grand Theft Auto 6 have a 99 Metascore, signaling "universal acclaim," according to Metacritic. The achievement puts GTA 6 atop a very strong top 10 on Metacritic — and knocks another Rockstar Games release out of the site's top 10 list. Here's the current top 10 on Metacritic, as of Nov. 18, the day before Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launches: Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2 held the No. 10 position until today, with its 97 Metascore. In Polygon's review of GTA 6 , critic Giovanni Colantonio lauded the game for its immersion, storytelling, and depth. "GTA once again earns its title as public enemy #1 — only this time, Rockstar accomplishes that less through bloodshed and more with an empathetic love story built for an era of stark economic uncertainty," Colantonio wrote. "It’s a bold choice, considering the series’ cold-blooded reputation, but it’s also what makes GTA 6 one of Rockstar’s finest games to date." Grand Theft Auto 6 was nominated for eight awards , including Game of the Year, at this year's The Game Awards on Tuesday, making it an early frontrunner for multiple GOTY awards. Ahead of launch, the game has reportedly sold more than 17 million copies, according to Sensor Tower , earning $1.65 billion in revenue for Rockstar Games and publisher Take-Two Interactive. Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launches on Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

The highly anticipated game, launching tomorrow (November 19), was also nominated for Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Performance (Manni L. Perez as Lucia Caminos), and Best Action/Adventure. Remedy's Control Resonant and Capcom's Resident Evil Requiem each earned six nominations, including Game of the Year. Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, IO Interactive's 007 First Light, and House House's Big Walk were each nominated in four categories. Zelda and First Light were also recognised for Game of the Year. Nintendo led all publishers with 12 nominations, followed by Capcom with 11, and Annapurna Interactive and PlayStation with nine each. This year, 112 games, individuals, and teams were nominated, selected by "a global jury of over 160 media publications and creator outlets." The Game Awards 2026 will take place on Thursday, December 10 at the Peacock Theatre in Los Angeles and will be broadcast on 40 digital streaming platforms, including Prime Video, Disney+, Twitch, and YouTube. At last year's ceremony, Sandfall Interactive's Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 won nine awards , including Game of the Year, after receiving 12 nominations . sources.text: The Game Awards says its judges "may be provided with advance or pre-release access to games for critical evaluation." The Game Awards has announced its nominations slate for 2026, revealing that Grand Theft Auto 6 is this year's most-nominated game. Rockstar's hotly anticipated crime epic has secured eight nominations including Game of the Year, for which it'll be competing with games including Resident Evil Requiem, Control Resonant, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Now you—and the countless other people preparing to argue about this online—may have noticed that GTA 6 has been nominated for a number of awards despite the fact that it hasn't been released yet . In a press release, The Game Awards notes that jurors were in some cases provided with early access to enable awards consideration. "The nominees for The Game Awards are selected by a global jury of over 160 media publications and creator outlets around the world, who may be provided with advance or pre-release access to games for critical evaluation," The Game Awards said. In a Variety interview last week, Game Awards host and co-creator Geoff Keighley refuted speculation that TGA 2026 eligibility deadlines had been sculpted to allow GTA 6 to have a shot for this year's nominations. "There was a thing a few weeks ago where everyone thought that we had changed our dates to accommodate GTA, and it's like, no, actually our dates have been very set every year. It's the same calendar that we have," Keighley said. "I don't know this, but I'm sure some of these companies consider that when they're looking at their release calendars." sources.title: First details on MLB The Show 27
sources.text: Includes the return of Now & Later Packs, MLB The Show 26 community stats, and more. Before we dive into new information on MLB The Show 27, let’s take a look back. As we reflect on 2026, two things stand out above everything else: the incredible passion and support of the MLB The Show community, and our need to better communicate and react to community feedback going forward. Whether you’ve been playing for decades or joined us for the first time this year, you’ve helped make this another special chapter in our franchise’s history. While we’re proud of what our team accomplished this year, we recognize that the heart of MLB The Show has always been its community. Since launch, you’ve hit an astonishing: You’ve also drawn 123,300,616 walks and racked up a staggering 2,130,551,161 strikeouts. It seems we have some work to do on our collective plate discipline and pitch recognition! But it’s not all strikeouts. You’ve also recorded 18,666,758 Perfect-Perfect hits and scored an incredible 2,506,757,548 runs. And if those numbers weren’t impressive enough, the community collectively spent the equivalent of 31,541 years playing MLB The Show this year. This year was not without some issues and hopefully over the next few months we’ll show you how we’ve made improvements in a host of areas.Your stories, feedback, creativity, and passion remind us why we do what we do. We don’t take your time, trust, or support for granted, and we’re incredibly fortunate to have a community that cares so deeply about the game. From all of us at San Diego Studio, thank you for another unforgettable year. We’re excited about what lies ahead and look forward to continuing this journey together. So, what lies ahead? We’re eager to share the exciting new features and improvements coming to MLB The Show 27, but it’s still a little too early to reveal what’s in store. However, there’s one announcement we can’t wait to make: The Tech Test is officially returning for MLB The Show 27. Tech Tests are invaluable to the development process. They help our team identify bugs, evaluate performance, and gather meaningful feedback from the community before the game officially launches. Now, you might be wondering: If Tech Tests are so important, why haven’t we held one since MLB The Show 23? That’s a fair question. Game development is challenging, and each year brings its own set of difficult decisions and competing priorities. Some of those decisions resulted in us not holding Tech Tests for the past few years. We appreciate your patience, passion, and continued support, and we’re looking forward to having you be part of the process again. We will provide more details on the Tech Test in the new year. There is still more ahead for MLB The Show 26 , and the time you spend playing can give you a head start in MLB The Show 27. Now & Later packs are coming back. Now & Later Packs contain items you can use now in MLB The Show 26, with the added bonus of allowing you to redeem The Show Packs “later” in MLB The Show 27 at no additional cost. Each Now & Later Pack you earn playing Diamond Dynasty Content in MLB The Show 26 on console will give out a Now & Later voucher that will automatically be redeemed into The Show Packs when logging into MLB The Show 27 on console during its standard release. Make sure you log into ‘27 with the same account you used to earn Now & Later Packs in ‘26. While that’s all for today, in the meantime, get a head start and start earning those Now & Later Packs in MLB The Show 26. We look forward to sharing more soon and are excited about what’s to come in 2027. In the meantime, for the latest MLB The Show news, head to TheShow.com , sign up for The Scouting Report , and follow our official social channels.

sources.title: GTA 6 Really Is Better On PS5 Than Xbox
sources.text: If you’re planning to get Grand Theft Auto 6 at launch, you’ll be able to buy it on two consoles: PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. But while both are capable pieces of hardware, it sure seems like developer Rockstar Games has a preference between the two. Advertisements for the game have declared that it “plays best on PS5.” Sony has even gotten custom GTA 6 DualSense controllers in celebration of the launch. To some, it could look like GTA 6 is a PS5 exclusive, even though it very much is not. Now that I’ve finally played GTA 6 for myself, it’s very clear why Sony’s console is the center of attention. It’s not so much about raw power, though the PS5 Pro is likely the best way for the techiest gamers to play, until we get a PC port; it has more to do with the DualSense. GTA 6 feels like it was built with the controller and its unique features in mind, making it a stronger sales pitch for the PS5 than most of Sony’s actual exclusives. It’s just a shame it’s coming so late in the console’s life cycle. In terms of how GTA 6 runs on PS5, there are no real surprises there. I largely played on PS5 Pro, which was able to give me a relatively smooth 30 frames per second performance. I did experience some framerate dips during high-level police chases, but it otherwise impresses considering the sheer scale of the world and its high level of detail throughout. I’ve yet to test it on Xbox Series X, but there are no red flags here that suggest it might struggle on Microsoft’s console. (The Xbox Series S is a wildcard.) What was instantly more noticeable during my playthrough was how GTA 6 goes all-in on the DualSense, to the point where it feels like Rockstar built the game specifically around the controller. You can see that in the little details. For instance, Jason and Lucia have cell phones that they can bring up at any time to send texts, make calls, and check apps. The sounds from that phone come through the DualSense’s built-in speaker. If someone calls you, you’ll hear the ring from the controller instead of the TV. That makes it feel like you, the player, are literally holding that phone in your hands — a small but effective bit of immersion. In that same vein, Rockstar also goes all in on haptic feedback to great effect. When you’re swimming, for example, you can feel each individual stroke Jason or Lucia takes. Again, much of the game feels like it was designed with that level of detail in mind. When cloning a car key, you’ll need to move the right joystick around in a circle and find the strongest vibration point. As you can imagine, haptic feedback only makes that minigame that much more tactile. Even the DualSense’s adaptive triggers get put to good use. Step on the gas in a car, and you’ll get a hit of resistance that simulates the feeling of stepping on a gas pedal. Crack open a shipping container with a saw, and you’ll need to very carefully increase pressure on the right trigger to make the cut. Stop to meditate, and you’ll feel the triggers rattle under your fingers as you press them to breathe in and out. Every little minigame interaction plays with the triggers or feedback in some way. The more I played, the more GTA 6 reminded me of early-generation PS5 tech showpieces; it has the same toy-like quality that Returnal and Astro’s Playroom had in the early PS5 years. While there have been plenty of third-party games that have integrated the DualSense in their own ways, GTA 6 has the most fully realized implementation of its features outside of Sony’s first-party games. That’s why it almost feels like an exclusive; six years into the PS5’s life, we finally have the game that really sells how the tech. None of that is necessary to enjoy GTA 6 , mind you. The extra feedback is a great perk if you own a PS5 already, but you’re not going to miss anything because your in-game phone rings from your TV speakers instead of your controller. The Xbox Series X will likely get the job done, and you might even prefer it if you don’t love the occasional strain that comes with adaptive triggers. But when Sony says that GTA 6 plays best on PS5, it’s not exactly a bluff. It does, but "play” is the key word there. It’s not that it looks or runs the best on PS5. It’s just the best platform for those who love toying around with their games.

The mission begins with meeting Brian at the bar. Then, follow Brian to his truck, and drive to the liquor store. Here youâll collect Cal, and head towards the next mission marker. sources.text: Head down to the depths of Leonida with Island Dreams Island Dreams is the ninth mission of this GTA 6 walkthrough. In this guide, weâll explain everything you need to know about the Island Dreams mission, highlight any collectibles and explain any choices that can be made as part of the mission. Our GTA 6 guides hub is the most comprehensive place to find all of our coverage of the game. In our complete walkthrough of GTA 6, weâre striving to avoid spoilers as much as possible. Island Dreams starts at Kentonâs shop, to the north of the keys. Speak to Kenton and heâll explain that the waters around Leonida are full of treasure, all of which can be sold for a high price. Kenton tells Jason that he can use his boat, and scuba gear, but first, he must escort a bachelor party on a scuba diving expedition. Get in the boat, and sail out to the map marker. When you get to the map marker, youâll be prompted to put on the scuba gear. Unlike a lot of the gear in GTA 6, scuba gear is only equipped while youâre in the water, or in a boat in the open water. If you return to land for too long, it will automatically unequip itself, as will metal detector and bolt gun. While swimming, you can use L3 to swim faster, and L2 to strafe while youâre in the water. In this mission, you need to escort the bachelor party through the trench. Once you get to the shipwreck, equip the metal detector. The metal detector is used to find treasure, and will flash green when youâre pointing it near a treasure site. As you get closer to the treasure, the green flash will increase in frequency, until eventually youâre given a prompt to use the triangle button to collect whatever youâve found. For this mission, youâll collect a couple of gold doubloons while the bachelor party hangs around the shipwreck. Gold doubloons are one of the gameâs resources that can be found all over the underwater segments of the map, and then sold to Kenton. After a while, youâll get a prompt to rescue Dobbs, as heâs managed to get himself stuck in the shipwreck. Donât worry if youâve not collected all the treasure at this wreck, as once youâve finished this mission, the game will allow you to revisit this and several other shipwrecks across the game to collect all of the treasure. Rescue Dobbs, and head back towards Kentonâs ship on the surface. As you do this, a shark will appear. Equip the spear gun and shoot the shark in the head. Be aware that the spear gun has a pretty aggressive arc if you shoot it too far from the shark, so make sure itâs close enough or your shots will fall short. After the shark is dead, go back to the surface, and watch the cutscenes to finish the Island Dreams mission in GTA 6. sources.title: Como GTA 6 roda no Xbox Series X, S, PS5 e PS5 Pro? A Rockstar explica
sources.text: GTA 6 vai ter carros (e ‘supercarros’) inspirados em modelos da vida real Rockstar mantém tradição que vem desde GTA 3, de 2001. GTA 6 foi lançado com uma empolgação descomunal por parte do público, mas muitos jogadores ficaram apreensivos com o fato de o game ser travado a 30 FPS nos atuais consoles. Em uma entrevista ao site Wccftech , os desenvolvedores da Rockstar Games explicaram essa motivação e como o jogo roda em diferentes consoles . Para cada videogame, a desenvolvedora afirma que selecionou uma combinação de diversas abordagens que conseguisse transmitir o visual e o desempenho almejado. O PlayStation 5 Pro tecnicamente é o console que melhor roda o título graças ao hardware levemente superior ao do PS5 base e do Xbox Series X. A informação sobre o Xbox Series S é bem interessante, já que o FSR 4 da AMD chegou ao Xbox há pouco mais de uma semana e nenhum jogo tinha exibido essa implementação até agora. Isso mostra como a parceria da AMD com os consoles da Microsoft tem se mostrado importante, especialmente no console com menor poder de fogo da geração. Jonathon Ashcroft (VP sênior de tecnologia), Chris Oat (diretor técnico de gráficos e engine) e Marc Chambers (diretor de produção de tecnologia) apontam que a escolha pelos 30 FPS em GTA 6 se deu logo no início do desenvolvimento do projeto. A razão é que a Rockstar quis equilibrar o peso da simulação, dos sistemas e da apresentação visual de Leonida . Para atingir esse nível de detalhes, a equipe precisou sacrificar a performance. Mesmo assim, eles afirmam que essa trava na taxa de quadros não prejudicará a precisão dos controles nos consoles. O estúdio garante que dedicou um tempo substancial para melhorar drasticamente a latência dos comandos do título, prometendo um tempo de resposta até superior ao encontrado em GTA 5 e Red Dead Redemption 2. Do ponto de vista gráfico, os desenvolvedores pontuam que o maior salto geracional de GTA 6 está na iluminação . Todo o pipeline de renderização e processamento de quadros foi construído já com suporte nativo ao HDR e SDR. O estúdio também implementou uma biblioteca de materiais físicos para garantir superfícies mais reais, como a pele molhada de um jacaré e tecidos de roupas em uma boate. Um dos objetivos da companhia é fazer com que os materiais e objetos presentes no jogo reajam à luz de acordo com as leis da física do mundo real. A imagem ainda passa por um tratamento que simula câmeras e lentes de cinema. Para ajudar nesse processo, a Rockstar implementou a tecnologia de Iluminação Global por Ray Tracing (RTGI) em todos os consoles . O Xbox Series S foi o que apresentou mais dificuldades por conta das limitações de memória RAM, mas o desafio foi superado. Os recursos foram balanceados individualmente para extrair a melhor representação de cada hardware, segundo a empresa. Por falar em GTA 6, o lançamento da Rockstar estreou com nota 99 no Metacritic e superou o clássico The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time de 1998.
