sources.title: GTA 6 looks gorgeous, and seeing it run at a stable 30 fps on ageing PS5 Pro hardware makes me hopeful for PC performance
sources.text: A stable 30 fps on RDNA 2 hardware with a game this stunning is promising. From what we're already seeing of Grand Theft Auto 6 on console, it's boding very well for a future PC release. It might only be targeting 30 fps on console, but with how stable that is and with the graphics looking so stunning on older PS5/PS5 Pro hardware, I've got high hopes for how it might run on our gaming PCs. Digital Foundry (DF) has taken one for the team here by doing some performance testing on an inferior platform (cheap shot, I'm sorry). And judging from the screenshots, videos, and frame rate analysis so far, GTA 6 looks very much next-gen in terms of scale, scope, and fidelity. We're talking fine detail on the local scale combined with open, bustling sight lines to the horizon, depending on your vantage point. All very noticeably saturated by incredible ray traced lighting, and running at a stable 30 fps on the PS5 Pro. It's hard to describe how fantastic GTA looks. It does seem like a new era for open world games. What particularly impresses me, judging from DF's gameplay and graphics shots, is how seamlessly fine detail combines with great lighting and breaks into long distance views. One minute you're inside a bustling store, with incredibly realistic ambient lighting and reflections thanks to the ray tracing implementation (plus ray traced shadows on the PS5 Pro), admiring the stranded hair on all the NPCs and the little touches such as drinks actually draining in the bottle you drink from. The next, you can be looking across the entire city without losing any noticeable detail. This seamlessness does make it seem like a real, lively world. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. A large part of this immersion seems to come from the lighting. You're getting full ray traced global illumination, apparently at 1440p resolution which, on the PS5 Pro, reportedly looks more like 4K (and on the base PS5 apparently looks like it might be 1440p upscaled). The PS5 (non-Pro) version looks a little more blurry and lacks the level of shadow definition, but for the most part both versions look great. At least as far as I can tell from DF's footage, anyway. All of the above is only good news if it runs well, and thankfully on this front it looks like it does. Yes, we're only talking 30 fps, but on the PS5 Pro version, at least, that's a very stable 30 fps. DF says there wasn't a single noticeable stutter or drop in over 50 hours of gameplay, and it's only when you start blowing up cars on the street that you get brief drops down to as low as 24 fps. The PS5 (non-Pro) is different, struggling to consistently maintain 30 fps even when just driving around the city. But that console has significantly worse hardware compared to the Pro, so it's to be expected—the GPU in the PS5 has just 36 compute units (CUs) compared to the PS5 Pro's 60. As far as playing GTA 6 on PC is concerned, I think this means we can be hopeful. The PS5 Pro's AMD GPU does have some RDNA 3/4 features, but for the most part it's an RDNA 2 chip. RDNA 2 graphics cards for PC are Radeon RX 6000-series ones. So, even with an older PC using a graphics card that is two generations old, it's possible you'll be able to get the gorgeous graphics you see on the PS5 Pro at a stable 30 fps. At what settings? Well, that remains to be seen. But considering we'll almost certainly get some more customisation options over on PC, we should be able to eke out as much performance as we can from it, tailored to our hardware. If you have a newer PC with a newer graphics card, I'd be hoping for 60 fps+ performance, and for that to be stable. The RX 9070 XT , for instance, should outperform a PS5 Pro considerably, despite only having a handful of extra CUs, thanks to the much newer architecture a higher power limit. Particularly promising is just how stable that 30 fps seems to be on the PS5 Pro. People often think about the average, but don't consider frame pacing and 1% lows. On those fronts, GTA 6 seems very well optimised. Our Chris has spent 100 hours with the Playstation 5 version of GTA 6 , and has come away with some very positive impressions. Here's hoping the PC release lives up to the hype, and that those of us on older rigs might be able to get in on the action without too many pricey upgrades. 4. sources.title: Rockstar says PS5 Pro can’t handle GTA 6 at 60 FPS
sources.text: Don’t hold your breath for a 60 FPS update for GTA 6 Rockstar has suggested that Grand Theft Auto 6 won’t get 60 FPS support post-launch, even on PlayStation 5 Pro. This was confirmed in a statement to Kotaku , with Rockstar ‘s technology production directorÂ Marc Chambers arguing that the PS5 Pro wouldn’t be capable of getting the game to run at 60 FPS. “Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination,” Chambers told Kotaku. “On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). “The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the gameâs visual fidelity.” With Chambers describing this as the “base” presentation for GTA 6 on PS5 Pro, it doesn’t sound like Rockstar is willing to turn down graphics settings on the platform to secure a higher frame rate. As it stands, he says that the PS5 Pro couldn’t go above 30 FPS with these settings. “While the PS5 Proâs central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the gameâs complex simulation at higher frame rates,” he says. 60 FPS has largely been seen as the industry standard for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S releases. The Blood of Dawnwalker almost released with a 30 FPS cap, but announced a 60 FPS performance mode prior to launch , following pushback online. Other games that launched at 30 FPS went on to get 60 FPS modes added post-launch, like Cyberpunk 2077 . The good news is that GTA 6 can at least maintain 30 FPS on the PS5 Pro , regardless of what the player is doing. That is at least according to analysis from Digital Foundry. However, they found that there were more frame rate dips on the base PS5, even in normal gameplay. One platform that Rockstar was willing to compromise on was the Xbox Series S. There are noticeably fewer details in this version of the game, but it still suffers from frame rate drops .

sources.title: Já é GTA VI na Austrália!
sources.text: A Rockstar Games lança nesta quinta-feira (19) Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) para PlayStation e Xbox , marcando a primeira nova história da franquia em 13 anos. O jogo já foi lançado na Austrália e soma 15 milhões de reservas antecipadas em todo o globo. Com potencial para movimentar bilhões de dólares e estabelecer novos padrões na indústria, o lançamento mobiliza milhões de jogadores. Segundo estimativas da Wedbush Securities, o título pode superar 30 milhões de unidades vendidas e US$ 3 bilhões (R$ 17,1 bilhões) em receita até o fim do ano. O Olhar Digital também acompanhará o lançamento de perto. Nossa equipe irá testar GTA 6 durante a madrugada, com a publicação das primeiras impressões na manhã seguinte. Um review completo do jogo está previsto para a próxima semana. Caso as reservas antecipadas alcancem 20 milhões nesta semana, como muitos esperam, as vendas se aproximarão de US$ 2 bilhões (R$ 11,4 bilhões). O interesse também aparece na preferência pelas versões do jogo: os pedidos estão concentrados principalmente na edição aprimorada, de US$ 99,99 (cerca de R$ 569,94), em vez da versão padrão, de US$ 79,99 (cerca de R$ 455,94). Os dados de pré-venda são da consultoria Sensor Tower. Para Joost van Dreunen, professor de negócios da Universidade de Nova York e especialista na indústria de videogames, o lançamento ultrapassa as dimensões habituais do setor. “Em 19 de novembro, veremos o maior lançamento de qualquer tipo de propriedade intelectual de entretenimento na história da humanidade”, afirmou ao The New York Times . A expectativa tem como referência o desempenho de Grand Theft Auto V , que vendeu mais de 30 milhões de cópias em 2013 e outras 200 milhões nos anos seguintes. A analista Alicia Reese, da Wedbush Securities, compara o potencial comercial da sequência ao sucesso de grandes produções cinematográficas. A arrecadação mundial de US$ 1,8 bilhão (R$ 10,26 bilhões) de The Odyssey , de Christopher Nolan, poderia equivaler aproximadamente à receita do primeiro dia de GTA 6 . A nova aventura retorna a Vice City, versão fictícia de Miami, e às regiões ao redor da cidade, no estado tropical imaginário de Leonida. Com mais de 200 GB, o jogo exige horas de download e apresenta um mundo aberto que vai além de perseguições de carros e tiroteios. Os jogadores poderão cumprir missões, explorar atividades paralelas, acessar estações de rádio próprias e acompanhar personagens secundários em suas rotinas. Entre os detalhes previstos estão fotografias emolduradas dos animais de estimação dos personagens, encontradas nas casas que eles habitam. “Dirigir e atirar fazem parte disso, mas não é mais apenas isso”, afirmou Mia Consalvo, professora de estudos de comunicação da Universidade Concordia, em Montreal. Para ela, a cidade reage às ações dos jogadores, que também podem simplesmente explorar e existir naquele ambiente, sem necessariamente cumprir missões. Essa combinação de liberdade e violência faz parte da identidade da franquia desde suas origens. Criada por desenvolvedores escoceses e ingleses que buscavam romper com a estética de magos e guerreiros comum em outros gêneros, a série construiu uma representação satírica e brutal da criminalidade urbana americana. A violência explícita, a representação de crimes e a presença de conteúdo sexual controverso também alimentaram críticas à franquia. Entre os episódios mais conhecidos está uma cena de sexo escondida em Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas , que provocou um escândalo. A expansão de Grand Theft Auto Online , modalidade multijogador de GTA V, também transformou o negócio da Rockstar. Especialmente durante a pandemia, a experiência ganhou popularidade ao permitir que jogadores interagissem em Los Santos, versão fictícia de Los Angeles. Dentro do ambiente virtual, é possível adquirir roupas, joias, carros, helicópteros, barcos e outros itens. Segundo a Wedbush Securities, a modalidade deve gerar mais de US$ 500 milhões (R$ 2,85 bilhões) em 2026 para a Rockstar e sua controladora, a Take-Two Interactive. A projeção é que a receita anual ultrapasse US$ 1 bilhão (R$ 5,7 bilhões) após o lançamento da versão online de GTA 6. O universo da franquia também abriu espaço para experiências artísticas. Durante a pandemia, os atores Sam Crane e Mark Oosterveen encenaram Hamlet dentro de GTA V. A produção, que utilizou diferentes cenários do jogo, deu origem ao documentário Grand Theft Hamlet , lançado em 2024. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo. sources.title: What are Criminal Profiles in GTA 6?
sources.text: Your Criminal Profile in Grand Theft Auto 6 is your reputation, similar to an honor or morality system Actions have consequences in Grand Theft Auto 6. Building on the honor system in Red Dead Redemption 2, fully functional Criminal Profiles in GTA 6 not only keep track of the way that you're playing the game, but help dictate how the world (and the characters who inhabit it) react to Jason and Lucia's presence. GTA 6 Criminal Profiles are a really important metric that can change fundamental aspects of your play experience. I'm going to help you understand all of this with an overview of the Criminal Profiles in GTA 6, and offer up some tips on how you can change through the five tiers. Your actions and behavior are captured in real-time by the Criminal Profile system. You are able to quickly check the status of your current criminal profile for both Jason and Lucia by holding right on the d-pad – look for the little icons next to their profile pictures for an update at a glance. For a deeper dive navigate to the "Jason & Lucia" menu. These profiles change over time, and their status can have a lasting impact on each of the characters so you will want to check this frequently. Jason and Lucia each have their own individual Criminal Profiles, but the actions of one character can influence the behavior of the other when you're out on the streets together. There are five Criminal Profiles in GTA 6 that Lucia and Jason can move between, all of which are laid out below from least to most severe. It's possible to move freely between Professional, Hardened, Violent, and Psycho tiers. However, should you create enough chaos to be considered Irredeemable this is an irreversible trait – and one which may permanently impact your relationship status in GTA 6. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Professional and Hardened Criminal Profiles are assigned to characters who do their best to avoid violence, and at least attempt to resolve situations without incident. Start pursuing extreme violence and cruelty to both animals and civilians and you'll become to etch into Violent and Psycho territories. While you're on a mission, Criminal Profiles aren't affected by any criminal acts that the game requires you to do. It's only when you go beyond what is truly necessary or reasonable that action begins to have consequences in either direction. Below your health bar is where the GTA 6 flashes up little icons which denote how your actions are impacting your criminal profile. The game will track low-casualty incursions and clean getaways, just as it will acts of extreme violence and destruction. If your character is going in a direction you aren't happy with, here's what to be aware of with each Criminal Profile: If you're after a Criminal Profile that lists you as a 'Professional' then you'll need to be considerate of your actions. Avoid casualties where possible, don't chase unnecessary aggression, and only do what could be considered reasonable to get the task at hand completed . It's worth noting that making threats won't impact your Professional Criminal Profile, and that the best way to maintain this reputation is to avoid violence unless you're threatened and to try to remain undetected while committing crimes. This isn't always possible, just don't escalate for the sake of it. Tip : Non-lethal incapacitations (aiming for joints rather than the head or heart), thoughtful actions, and petting every dog and cat you come across will increase your Focus in GTA 6 while you have a Professional Criminal Profile. If you've found yourself with a Hardened Criminal Profile in GTA 6, it probably means that you've started to resort to violence to complete your objectives. Rushing to kill enemies and breaking detection for the sake of it will contribute to this profile – although it's still easy enough to get back to a Professional Criminal Profile if you take steps to avoid violence in a couple of robberies. If you continue down this path, harming civilians and killing cops, then your Criminal Profile will eventually shift from Hardened to Violent. It's worth flagging that, like the Professional profile, non-lethal incapacitations will still contribute to an increase in your focus. If you've gotten yourself a Violent Criminal Profile in GTA 6 then something has gone really wrong. This is the game reflecting that you've probably spent a fair few hours attacking cops and civilians for the smallest infractions. Brutally attacking cops and shooting fleeing civilians in the back will contribute to your Violent profile but acting in a self-defensive capacity will not . If you find yourself pushing into Psycho territory, it is still possible to move back to Hardened or Professional. You'll just need to be more conscious about the way you are interacting with the world, and become more deliberate with your actions. Tip: Headshots will increase your focus if you've gotten yourself a Violent profile, but each one of those will also make it more difficult to return to Hardened or Professional state. You know what you're doing, and you don't care who knows about it. If you get assigned the Psycho Criminal Profile in GTA 6 then you've most likely spent a few hours mercilessly harming vulnerable animals (yes, hunting does count in certain instances), murdering defenseless civilians with abandon, and have been blasting through cops with no hesitation. Something to note with the Psycho profile is that there is an additional icon you should keep an eye out for. If you see a line-scratch through the icon, it means you've reached a breaking point and are at risk of tipping into Irredeemable territory. Start shooting to incapacitate to get back to being a reasonable member of society. If you continue acting with wild abandon once you reach the breaking point within the Psycho boundaries , eventually you will earn yourself an Irredeemable Criminal Profile in GTA 6.
